Stroke syndromes can present along a wide spectrum of disease from transient ischemic attacks with complete resolution of symptoms to large intracranial hemorrhages with uncal or tonsillar herniation. Embolic strokes tend to have a sudden onset, and neuroimaging may demonstrate previous infarcts in several vascular territories or may show calcific emboli. Cardioembolic strokes may be isolated, multiple and in a single hemisphere, or scattered and bilateral; the latter 2 types indicate multiple vascular distributions and are more specific for cardioembolism.
